summary: Restored sglang:avg_request_queue_latency as a live gauge computed from initialized wait_queue_entry_time values in the current scheduler waiting queue, using one shared allocation-free helper for prefill and decode reporting.

tests.what_was_measured: The issue-specific regression failed during collection because the queue-latency calculation did not exist in the prepared base.
Four deterministic numerical cases passed: mean current wait, empty queue, exclusion of an uninitialized timestamp, and clamping a future timestamp to zero.
Existing metrics wrapper compatibility: 33 tests and 4 subtests passed.

A source-checkout SGLang server on one gfx950 GPU returned HTTP 200 for two queued generation requests; /metrics simultaneously reported num_queue_reqs=1.0 and avg_request_queue_latency=0.003117550048045814.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-c031fac99fc2/evidence/server.log records real Triton gfx950 prefill/decode work; run-metadata.json records the successful queued HTTP requests and positive metric observation.
remaining_limitations: The deterministic random tiny Llama fixture validates only single-gfx950 transport, engine execution, and scheduler metric emission. The reported TP=8 DP-attention NVIDIA deployment, production weights/model semantics, and distributed behavior were not reproduced. No native C++ source changed. The probe server required SIGKILL after its graceful-shutdown timeout; its descendants were reaped and rocm-smi showed the assigned GPU idle afterward. Ruff was not installed in the required interpreter, so focused pytest, source execution, and git diff --check were used instead.
